In detail

Devon & Cornwall Police recorded 310 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 7.7 per 1,000 residents, the 12th highest rate of Plymouth's 20 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (8), drugs (3), burglary (2); the evening/night score by violent crime (45), public order (11), anti social behaviour (8). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Moor View safe?

Wandroz currently rates Moor View in Plymouth as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Plymouth during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Plymouth at night. This rating is derived from Devon & Cornwall Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Moor View safe at night?

At night, Moor View is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Plymouth. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Moor View a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Moor View's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Plymouth) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.
